title: Introduce weight demultiplexer service and decouple tokenizer lifecycle from weight activation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: Reduce model startup tail latency and simplify cross-format weight handling by extracting a lightweight weight demultiplexer (weight-demux) service and separating tokenizer initialization from final weight activation. This ticket covers the refactor, compatibility shim, migration tooling, benchmarks, and rollout plan. The change should make onboarding new checkpoint formats easier, reduce OOM spike during model activation, and enable faster cold start for short-lived inference containers.
background: Current bootstrap couples: (1) heavy-weight checkpoint parsing + sharded weight materialization, (2) tokenizer vocab resolution and pre-init, and (3) final weight activation. This coupling causes repeated code paths across loaders, fragile format-specific conditionals, and long tail latencies when loading large models with many shards. Past attempts to "streamline" the ingest left format-specific logic spread across the loader and tokenizer subsystems. This refactor centralizes shard demux logic and introduces a clear contract between: weight-demux -> weight-hydrator -> runtime-activator, while the tokenizer lifecycle moves to an independent token-service that can be warmed in parallel or queried lazily.
acceptance_criteria: Weight demultiplexer packaged as an internal library/service with stable public APIs (installable via internal artifact registry)
Token lifecycle moved out of the critical activation path; containers cold-start 20-35% faster in 95th percentile latency for Llama-70B-like checkpoints in our benchmark cluster
No regression in unit/integration tests; end-to-end load tests pass on canary cluster
Migration script can convert existing manifests to the canonical demux manifest and run idempotently
Compatibility shim present to support legacy checkpoint formats during rollout
design_decisions: Introduce a minimal manifest format (demux.manifest.v1) that lists shard segments, preferred order, checksums, and loader hints. This keeps metadata small and avoids reading entire checkpoint headers to route streams.
Make weight-demux responsible only for sharding/destination mapping and checksum verification; actual byte decoding remains in existing format adapters to reduce rewrite scope.
Token-service will expose a compact HTTP/gRPC endpoint for vocab resolution and subword boundary queries; runtime will cache lookups locally with TTL-based invalidation.
Backward compatibility: a compatibility adapter layer will synthesize demux.manifest.v1 from legacy manifests on first use and persist the synthesized manifest to the model registry.
We will not change on-disk weight encodings in this rollout; quantization/encoding changes are out of scope and owned by runtime-quant team.
progress_updates: 2025-02-20: Spike complete. PoC demux library that reads a small manifest and emits shard streams. Measured 15% improvement in model activation path in dev harness (Ben)
2025-02-25: Architecture review with infra and runtime teams. Agreed to keep manifest v1 intentionally minimal; token-service will be optional prewarm (Lena + Ben)

2025-03-01: Initial compatibility shim implemented that converts legacy manifest formats from cataloged models; wrote migration script (scripts/migrate_to_demux.sh) and smoke-tested on internal staging (Aisha)

2025-03-04: Integration tests added for demux + hydrator handshake. Discovered a race when tokenizer prewarm completes after activator; added preactivation barrier and fallback path to query token-service lazily (Ben)
2025-03-06: Performance tuning: reduced memory peak by streaming checkpoints chunk-wise; 95p cold-start latency improved from 2.8s to 1.9s on staging (bench cluster run #20250306-alpha)
open_risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Some legacy manifests are malformed and rely on loading order side effects. Mitigation: compatibility shim runs in conservative mode and logs repair candidates; add a migration audit tool and opt-in repair flag.

Risk: Token-service availability could add external dependency at cold-start. Mitigation: make token-service optional and add runtime-local warm cache with LRU and prefetch heuristics; fall back to embedded tokenizer as last resort.

Risk: Increased deploy surface (demux + token-service). Mitigation: start as a library feature toggled per-model, then extract to service after stability; run canary on dedicated cluster nodes before full rollout.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for demux manifest parsing and shard routing. 2) Integration tests for hydrator handshake and tokenizer fallbacks. 3) End-to-end load tests against bench cluster for 20 representative checkpoints. 4) Canary rollout to 5% of production traffic with runtime-1.20 label, run A/B latency/cost regressions for 72h. 5) Post-mortem checklist if errors > 0.5% or latency regressions > 10% at p95.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Deploy library behind feature flag; run migration script on staging to verify synthesized manifests. Phase 2: Enable for low-traffic models and run canary. Phase 3: Sweep model registry to migrate remaining manifests during a scheduled maintenance window; provide fallback to synthesize on first load in emergency. Migration tool: internal repo GitHub: redwood-inference/model-tools PR #7654.
rollout_steps: Merge compatibility shim and demux library behind feature flag (PR #7654)
Run migration tool on staging registry and validate artifacts (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/x/LoadDemux-Design)
Deploy token-service as optional prewarm on canary nodes (runtime-1.20-canary)
Start 5% traffic canary for 72h, monitor p50/p95 cold starts and unit cost (console dashboard: /dashboards/model-load)
Gradually increase to 100% with rollback window and playbook ready
next_actions: Finish edge-case handling for malformed legacy manifests (due 2025-03-10)
Add synthetic manifest publisher to model registry (due 2025-03-12)
Prepare rollback playbook and notify SRE and support teams
notes: This ticket intentionally avoids heavy refactors of checkpoint deserializers. The primary value is architectural separation of concerns: routing/manifesting vs decoding vs token vocab management. We expect follow-up tickets to extract additional format adapters and introduce a streaming protocol for inter-node shard fetches.
